provenance.note: Only visible report tables are extracted. Citation markers are preserved as source locators, not resolved or independently verified.

functions.name: Sensory pleasure
functions.definition: Positive hedonic response to sensory qualities.
functions.research_anchor: Food and aesthetic research show sensory qualities as one component of reward. citeturn3search3turn8search2

functions.name: Savouring
functions.definition: Attending to, deepening or prolonging a positive experience.
functions.research_anchor: RCT meta-analysis supports savouring as a distinct positive-experience process. citeturn15search3

functions.name: Stimulation / arousal
functions.definition: Reward from activation, pace, energetic input or surprise.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not necessarily emotional intensity or risk.
functions.research_anchor: Music and horror research distinguish activation from other rewards. citeturn9search3turn9search0

functions.name: Emotional intensity
functions.definition: Valuing strong felt affect, including mixed emotion.
functions.research_anchor: Sad-music and aesthetics evidence demonstrates rewarding intense/mixed emotion. citeturn9search5turn8search2

functions.name: Mood/state regulation
functions.definition: Using experience to change, sustain or organise affect.
functions.research_anchor: Music meta-analyses and nature research support regulatory functions. citeturn9search4turn9search1turn13search8

functions.name: Restoration
functions.definition: Replenishment after cognitive, emotional or physical demands.
functions.research_anchor: Vacation and nature syntheses support recovery/restoration. citeturn14view6turn6search7

functions.name: Detachment / escape
functions.definition: Temporary psychological distance from demands or routine.
functions.research_anchor: Vacation and media/gaming literatures distinguish detachment from pathology. citeturn14view6turn7search0turn9search9

functions.name: Comfort/familiarity
functions.definition: Reward from predictability, ease and known patterns.
functions.research_anchor: Comfort-food and rewatching reviews support familiar-experience functions. citeturn5search1turn9search9

functions.name: Nostalgia/continuity
functions.definition: Reconnection with autobiographical or shared past.
functions.research_anchor: Sad-music and media-rewatching literature identifies nostalgia as one mechanism. citeturn9search5turn9search9

functions.name: Pleasure in movement
functions.definition: Intrinsic kinaesthetic enjoyment.
functions.research_anchor: Enjoyment is a recurrent physical-activity facilitator; dance work emphasises embodiment. citeturn4search0turn4search10

functions.name: Embodied intensity
functions.definition: Reward from strong bodily sensations or exertion.
functions.research_anchor: Adventure-sport and spicy-food reviews show heterogeneous pathways into intense bodily experiences. citeturn4search3turn5search3

functions.name: Challenge
functions.definition: Reward from tackling difficulty requiring effort/adaptation.
functions.research_anchor: Flow and sport research consistently implicate challenge. citeturn12search0turn4search0

functions.name: Mastery
functions.definition: Reward from progressively refining a skill.
functions.research_anchor: Competence/flow and gaming literature support skill refinement as motivating. citeturn14view0turn12search0turn14view8

functions.name: Achievement/progress
functions.definition: Reward from milestones, completion or measurable advancement.
functions.research_anchor: Achievement/goal orientation is recurrent in sport and gaming. citeturn4search0turn14view8

functions.name: Competence
functions.definition: Felt effectiveness when interacting with a task/environment.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not a judgement of global ability.
functions.research_anchor: A central basic psychological need in SDT evidence. citeturn14view0turn14view1

functions.name: Autonomy
functions.definition: Acting in a way experienced as volitional and self-endorsed.
functions.research_anchor: Strongly grounded in SDT evidence. citeturn14view0turn14view1
functions.cross_domain_example: road trip + side project + solo run

functions.name: Agency/control
functions.definition: Reward from shaping outcomes and observing effects of one's actions.
functions.research_anchor: Gaming and work research supports action/outcome control as a relevant affordance. citeturn14view8turn14view1

functions.name: Novelty
functions.definition: Reward from unfamiliarity or freshness.
functions.research_anchor: Novelty is implicated in curiosity and travel-related motivation. citeturn15search0turn6search6

functions.name: Exploration
functions.definition: Active search through environments or possibilities.
functions.research_anchor: Curiosity theory explicitly connects curiosity with exploratory behaviour. citeturn15search0

functions.name: Curiosity
functions.definition: Desire to resolve a knowledge/information gap.
functions.research_anchor: Current reviews directly support this distinction. citeturn15search0turn15search1

functions.name: Learning
functions.definition: Reward from acquiring skill, knowledge or perspective.
functions.research_anchor: Curiosity and reading evidence distinguish knowledge-seeking from acquisition. citeturn15search0turn3search5

functions.name: Cognitive complexity
functions.definition: Enjoyment of ambiguity, layered structure or interpretation.
functions.research_anchor: Aesthetic experience is strongly multidimensional and can involve ambiguity/interpretation. citeturn14view7turn8search2

functions.name: Flow/absorption
functions.definition: Deep involvement and intrinsically rewarding attentional absorption.
functions.research_anchor: Flow reviews consistently identify absorption alongside challenge, goals and feedback. citeturn12search0turn12search3

functions.name: Play
functions.definition: Voluntary experimentation, humour, imaginative variation or intrinsically enjoyable rule use.
functions.research_anchor: Gaming and leisure research support play as distinct from achievement. citeturn14view8turn13search7

functions.name: Competition
functions.definition: Reward from comparative contest or ranking.
functions.research_anchor: Competition appears independently from mastery/challenge in sport and gaming motivation. citeturn4search0turn14view8

functions.name: Creation
functions.definition: Reward from making or transforming something.
functions.research_anchor: Cooking/hobby evidence supports creation and self-efficacy-like rewards, though causality is uneven. citeturn5search2turn13search7

functions.name: Aesthetic pleasure
functions.definition: Reward from form, composition, style or material qualities.
functions.research_anchor: Contemporary aesthetics research rejects reduction of aesthetic experience to a single beauty dimension. citeturn14view7turn8search2

functions.name: Awe
functions.definition: Wonder/perspective shift elicited by perceived vastness or profundity.
functions.research_anchor: Experimental meta-analysis supports awe as a distinguishable emotion. citeturn2search1

functions.name: Meaning/reflection
functions.definition: Reward from significance, interpretation or connection to larger narratives.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not proof of spirituality or virtue.
functions.research_anchor: Narrative and aesthetic evidence supports reflective/meaning-oriented engagement. citeturn3search5turn8search1

functions.name: Self-expression/identity
functions.definition: Using choices to express or maintain a sense of self.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Never licence to infer sensitive identity.
functions.research_anchor: Identity-expressive consumption and music/media work support this function. citeturn8search14turn9search3

functions.name: Distinction/status signalling
functions.definition: Reward from communicating prestige, scarcity or social distinction.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not the default explanation for luxury.
functions.research_anchor: Luxury research establishes status signalling as one motive among several. citeturn8search11turn8search13

functions.name: Belonging
functions.definition: Inclusion and acceptance within a group or social world.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not intimacy with a particular person.
functions.research_anchor: Belonging and relatedness are well-supported constructs. citeturn11search5turn14view0

functions.name: Intimacy/attachment
functions.definition: Close particularised bond involving trust and mutual importance.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not group inclusion or crowd energy.
functions.research_anchor: Adult attachment research supports close-bond functions. citeturn11search2

functions.name: Care/contribution
functions.definition: Reward from supporting or nurturing another person's welfare.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not proof of self-sacrifice or moral virtue.
functions.research_anchor: Meta-analytic work on communal motivation supports caregiving-oriented motivation. citeturn11search9

functions.name: Shared experience
functions.definition: Value of co-experiencing something with another person/group.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not necessarily belonging or high arousal.
functions.research_anchor: Experiments show sharing can alter experience and can be sought for connection. citeturn10search0turn10search3

functions.name: Collective energy
functions.definition: High-arousal unison from synchronised attention/emotion/movement.
functions.research_anchor: Collective-effervescence meta-analysis supports this as a group-event process. citeturn7search1turn7search6

functions.name: Social observation/simulation
functions.definition: Reward from interpreting others' motives, relationships and behaviour.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not proof of empathy or social skill.
functions.research_anchor: Narrative-reading evidence shows small/context-sensitive social-cognitive effects. citeturn3search1turn3search4

functions.name: Ritual/structure
functions.definition: Reward from repeated ordered, meaningful sequences.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not mere familiarity and not compulsivity.
functions.research_anchor: Ritual review identifies emotional, goal-state and social regulation. citeturn15search2turn5search6

functions.name: Recognition/esteem
functions.definition: Reward from acknowledgement of contribution or performance.
functions.research_anchor: Work/social motivation research supports interpersonal acknowledgement as contextual reward, although it is less cleanly isolated than basic needs. citeturn14view1

functions.name: Nature connection
functions.definition: Reward from contact with landscapes and living/non-built environments.
functions.not_equivalent_to: Not synonymous with calmness or restoration.
functions.research_anchor: Nature syntheses show multiple affective and restorative pathways. citeturn6search2turn6search7turn13search8
